idiom_name: service struct with trait ports, sqlx Transaction passed as &mut
implementation_notes: Rust has no classes and no dependency-injection container, so the service is a struct holding its ports (trait objects or generic parameters) and the transaction is an explicit value: let mut tx = pool.begin().await?, queries execute against &mut *tx, and tx.commit().await? ends it - if the Transaction is dropped without committing, sqlx rolls back. Nothing replaces the classic structure; the compiler just enforces what other languages leave to convention, since the transaction's lifetime and the requirement to thread it through every call are checked at compile time. Async ports need async-trait or native async traits; generic ports monomorphise while dyn ports need Send + Sync for spawned futures.
pitfalls: A transaction dropped without commit rolls back silently, so an early ? return looks like success unless the error is propagated and handled.
Running a query against the pool instead of &mut tx escapes the transaction and can deadlock against its own locks.
Trait-object ports must be Send + Sync (and often 'static) before the resulting future can be spawned; generic parameters avoid the bounds at the cost of monomorphisation.
